proposal_topic_title: Category-Theoretic Invariants of Multi-Agent RL Policy Spaces
proposal_topic_intro:
Reinforcement learning policy spaces are high-dimensional objects whose geometry is poorly understood. Category-theoretic invariants---drawn from iquantum group representation theory and algebraic structures studied by Lab-Epsilon---may characterise which policy classes are equivalent under symmetry transformations, yielding provable convergence or robustness guarantees.

This is the most theoretically demanding proposal in the collaboration: only Epsilon's algebra work and, tangentially, Gamma's systematic KGE review are directly relevant. Alpha's voice-RL results, Beta's competitive offline RL, and Delta's sim-to-real transfer work are adjacent but not core to the category-theoretic framing.

participating_pis.research_summary: Alpha leads Lab-Alpha, studying speaker diarisation, blockchain authentication, and lifelong RL. The lab introduced text-based diarisation error metrics, the LoopSR lifelong policy adaptation framework for sim-to-real legged locomotion, and a blockchain-based authenticated voice system.

Beta leads Lab-Beta, focusing on sim-to-real RL transfer and multi-agent competitive RL. The lab developed LoopSR for legged locomotion, and Off-FSP, the first practical model-free offline RL algorithm for competitive multi-agent settings approximating Nash equilibrium on partially covered datasets.

Gamma leads Lab-Gamma, at the intersection of SNNs, RL, and knowledge graph embedding. The lab introduced AdaFire adaptive-firing neurons, Spiking Denoising Diffusion Probabilistic Models, the World Model-based Perception method for legged locomotion, and a systematic KGE review.

Delta leads Lab-Delta, specialising in agent-based modelling, RL, and robotics. The lab created the Relativitization open-source simulation of interstellar societies, developed BMPO bidirectional model-based policy optimisation, and introduced the Historical Information Bottleneck for sim-to-real policy transfer.

Epsilon leads Lab-Epsilon, working on algebra-inspired ML and information retrieval. The lab contributed to iquantum group theory and relative braid group actions, developed IRGAN for information retrieval using GANs, and built statistical-arbitrage ML for online advertising optimisation.
